title: Étale recovery of the closed exceptional quotient comparison
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell
e\operatorname{char}k$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $1\le m\le n$, $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $B=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, with the quotient map. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. On the ordinary small étale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] let $G_R=Ri_{R,\mathrm{et}}^!$ be the right adjoint to $i_{*,R}$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient], for $R=A,B$. On the pro-étale constructible realization use its transport [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] along $
u_W:W_{\mathrm{proet}}	o W_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Put $T=-\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. If $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ (bounded constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] with a finite Tor interval: some integers $a\le b$ satisfy $\mathcal H^r(M\otimes_A^LF)=0$ for every degree-zero $A$-module sheaf $F$ and every $r
otin[a,b]$), then both $TG_AM$ and $G_BTM$ are in $D^b_{ctf}(Z_{\mathrm{et}},B)$, and the étale exceptional-counit transpose
$$b^{\mathrm{et}}_{i,M}:TG_AM\longrightarrow G_BTM$$
is an isomorphism. Under the tensor pullback and transported exceptional identifications its pullback $
u_Z^*b^{\mathrm{et}}_{i,M}$ equals the pro-étale map of [lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek] at $
u_X^*M$. Here the defining transpose is $i_{*,B}TG_AM\xrightarrow{c^{-1}}T i_{*,A}G_AM\xrightarrow{T\varepsilon_A}TM$, where $c$ is the canonical closed-direct-image coefficient comparison. Equality of diagrams between these bounded-below étale outputs can be tested after applying $
u_Z^*$.

proof.text: Put $C=\nu^*$, $N=G_AM$, $M_B=TM$. Finite type over $k$ makes $X,Z$ Noetherian. The cited etale closed-preservation clause at levels $n,m$ gives $N,G_BM_B$ finite-Tor constructible; the input-model theorem on $M,N$ gives $M_B,TN$ with the same Tor intervals and bounded K-flat representatives on both sites, without flatness of $B/A$. Comparison preserves these intervals. Write $t_{W,K}:C_BTK\cong T^pC_AK$ for tensor pullback and $e_{R,L}:C_RG_RL\cong G_R^pC_RL$ for exceptional transport through the comparison unit. All outputs are bounded below.

proof.text:
Closed immersions are proper, so use $h=i,c=(\mathrm{id},i)$ in [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. Its $\beta,b$ are the counit-transpose coefficient maps $c^e,c^p$; its $c^c$ is the ordinary counit-mate $\delta$, and its tensor comparison is $t^{-1}$. Thus its square rearranges to
$$i_*^p(t_{Z,N})\delta_{B,TN}C_B(c^e)=c^pT^p(\delta_{A,N})t_{X,i_*N}.$$
The direct-image coefficient theorem also gives both inverses for the cyclic $A$-module $B$.

proof.text:
Define $b^e$ by $T\varepsilon_A^e(c^e)^{-1}$. By [lem-coef-site-closed-counit-transport], in the $e$ coordinates the counit is $\varepsilon_R^p=C_R(\varepsilon_R^e)\delta_R^{-1}$ and adjuncts are transported by $C$. Consequently the transpose of $C_B(b^e)t_{Z,N}^{-1}$, after $t_{X,M}$, is
$$t_{X,M}C_B(T\varepsilon_A^e)C_B(c^e)^{-1}\delta_{B,TN}^{-1}i_*^p(t_{Z,N}^{-1})
=T^p(C_A\varepsilon_A^e)t_{X,i_*N}C_B(c^e)^{-1}\delta_{B,TN}^{-1}i_*^p(t_{Z,N}^{-1})
=T^p(C_A\varepsilon_A^e\delta_{A,N}^{-1})(c^p)^{-1}.$$
The first equality is naturality of $t$, the second the inverted step-2 square. This is the defining transpose of [lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek]; injectivity of the transported Hom bijection identifies the maps.

proof.text: The input $C_{X,A}M$ is finite-Tor constructible by step 1, and $i$ and $A\to B$ meet all the geometric and coefficient hypotheses of [lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek]. That theorem makes the pro-etale map of step 3 invertible. By [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], $C_{Z,B}$ is fully faithful on $D^+$, which contains both etale outputs by step 1. Fullness lifts the inverse of its image; faithfulness reflects the two inverse equations, so $b^e$ is invertible. For two paths between bounded-below etale outputs, faithfulness likewise reflects equality of their images. This proves the isomorphism, its asserted pro-etale identification, and the diagram test.
